clue.text: Gadget design, a raincoat with everything used in Intelligence

indicators.note: things used in something are put inside it, so these pieces go within the intelligence word

parts.note: wit is intelligence or quickness of mind
to hatch is to devise or design (a plot)
a mac is a mackintosh, a raincoat
all means everything

explanation.surface: A product description: some clever gizmo built from a raincoat, with every feature, deployed by the intelligence services.
explanation.walkthrough: 'design' looks like a noun beside 'Gadget' but is the verb hatch, as in hatching a plot; the intelligence word splits around the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A whatchamacallit is an informal name for any object whose proper name escapes you, typically a gadget or gizmo.

clue.text: One male, large in underwear, finding chest expanders?

parts.note: one as the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: in says the large letter goes inside the underwear word

parts.note: pants are underwear
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A man in his underwear discovering a cosmetic enhancement, told with a nudge.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a playful definition: breast implants literally expand the chest.
explanation.definitionFit: Breast implants are surgical inserts that enlarge the bust, humorously called devices for expanding the chest.

clue.text: Marker at sea young chap picked up

indicators.note: picked up means heard, as on a radio, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a boy is a young chap

explanation.surface: A sailor spotting a navigation marker, or a lad being collected from the water.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech the floating marker is often pronounced like 'boy'.
explanation.definitionFit: A buoy is a floating object anchored to mark a channel or hazard for shipping.

clue.text: Books with huge topless woman, making you blind?

indicators.note: topless drops the first letter, the top of a down entry

parts.note: big means huge
Nora is a woman's name
NT is the New Testament, a collection of books

explanation.surface: A saucy warning that ogling a giant topless woman in a book might cost you your sight.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface plays on the old warning that certain vices make you go blind; the definition is the figurative sense of blind.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone figuratively blind to a fact is unaware of it, lacking knowledge of it.

clue.text: Constant frost beginning to abate where Russians in occupation

parts.note: C is the symbol for a constant, as in physics (speed of light)
rime is hoar frost

indicators.note: beginning to picks the first letter of abate

parts.note: first letter gives A

explanation.surface: A weather report: a persistent frost starting to ease.
explanation.walkthrough: Russia annexed the Crimean peninsula in 2014 and holds it still.
explanation.definitionFit: Crimea is a Black Sea peninsula occupied by Russian forces since its annexation from Ukraine in 2014.

clue.text: Hanger-on right to stop balance being disturbed

indicators.note: to stop means to plug a gap, so the right letter goes into the reworked letters of the other word
being disturbed says the letters are thrown into disorder and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone clinging on beside you with a right-hand blow that upsets your balance.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange BALANCE as BANACLE ('being disturbed'), then R plugs it after BA ('to stop').
explanation.definitionFit: A barnacle is a crustacean that clings to rocks and hulls, so figuratively a person who sticks to another.

clue.text: Antlered animal the thing with one furry foot raised

indicators.note: raised in a down entry means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: it is the thing
one as the Roman numeral I
a paw is an animal's furry foot

explanation.surface: A deer described as lifting one furry hoof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns ITIPAW upwards in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: The wapiti is a large North American deer, the elk, whose males carry big antlers.

clue.text: Dope on bed — is it Murray arrested by fat detectives here?

parts.note: dope is slang for information, news
a cot is a bed

indicators.note: arrested by means held inside

parts.note: lard is pig fat
Andy Murray is the tennis player, so his first name

explanation.surface: A tabloid headline asking whether Murray has been nicked by the detectives, with the gossip on the bed.
explanation.walkthrough: Andy Murray is the Scottish tennis champion; 'is it Murray' hints at his first name, held inside LARD.
explanation.definitionFit: New Scotland Yard is the headquarters of London's Metropolitan Police, the home of its CID detectives.

clue.text: German meat cured on food that needs sending back

parts.note: ham is meat that has been cured

indicators.note: sending back means read backwards

parts.note: re means on, concerning
grub is food

explanation.surface: A German sausage-maker complaining about food that ought to be returned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German meat' reads as one phrase; 'German' alone is the definition, a citizen of Hamburg.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hamburger is a native or inhabitant of the city of Hamburg, so a German.

clue.text: Current period, and lengthy one for gnome?

parts.note: AD (Anno Domini) is the current era
an age is a lengthy period

explanation.surface: A question about eras, current and long, with a gnome tossed in as if a garden figure.
explanation.walkthrough: A gnome is also a pithy saying, as in the adjective gnomic.
explanation.definitionFit: A gnome in this sense is a maxim or aphorism, and an adage is just such a traditional saying.

clue.text: Agree with Home Office: shout to identify quarry

parts.note: to tally is to agree, match
HO is the abbreviation for the Home Office, the UK ministry for policing and immigration

explanation.surface: Politicians agreeing with a government department before a hunt starts.
explanation.definitionFit: Tally-ho is the cry fox hunters give when they sight the fox they are chasing.

clue.text: People baptise sons in hilly region

parts.note: men are people
to dip is to immerse, as in baptism
S is the abbreviation for son(s)

explanation.surface: A rural scene of folk baptising their boys out in the hills.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mendips are a range of limestone hills in Somerset, England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mendip Hills, or Mendips, are a limestone upland in Somerset in south-west England.

clue.text: Note placed in cabin for Chancellor

indicators.note: placed in puts one letter inside the other word

parts.note: a hut is a cabin

explanation.surface: A memo left in a holiday cabin for the finance minister.
explanation.walkthrough: Jeremy Hunt was the UK Chancellor of the Exchequer (finance minister) in 2022 to 2024.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeremy Hunt served as Chancellor of the Exchequer, Britain's finance minister.

clue.text: Spoil cotton clothing while making liqueur

indicators.note: clothing means wrapping around, so the words around hold the while word

parts.note: to mar is to spoil
chino is a cotton twill fabric
as means while

explanation.surface: Spilling a drink on cotton clothes while mixing a liqueur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothing' looks like garments, but it is the verb: the spoil-and-cotton pair wraps around the word for while. Chinos are cotton twill trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: Maraschino is a clear cherry liqueur from the Dalmatian marasca cherry.

clue.text: Rodent from Welsh river runs, coming aboard coaster?

indicators.note: coming aboard puts these letters inside the other word

parts.note: a coaster is a drinks mat
the Usk is a river in Wales
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A rodent from a Welsh river scrambling aboard a coastal vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coaster' suggests a ship, to go with 'aboard', but here it is a drinks mat.
explanation.definitionFit: The muskrat is a large aquatic rodent of North America.

clue.text: Goat perhaps having drink at home with social worker

parts.note: rum is a drink
in means at home
an ant is a social insect and a worker

explanation.surface: A goat having a drink at home with a social worker.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'social worker' is a worker ant, ants being social insects.
explanation.definitionFit: Goats chew the cud, so a goat is an example of a ruminant; 'perhaps' marks the example.

clue.text: Prove superior as cleric filling bucket

indicators.note: filling means going inside

parts.note: a pail is a bucket
Rev is short for Reverend, a cleric

explanation.surface: A clergyman triumphing by stuffing himself into a bucket.
explanation.definitionFit: To prevail is to win out or triumph, showing oneself the stronger.

clue.text: Page with Lima in the map redrawn for publication

indicators.note: redrawn says the letters are rearranged, like a map drawn afresh

parts.note: Lima is L in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A cartographer's page placing Lima on a revised map for publication.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lima' suggests the Peruvian capital but is the radio-alphabet L; 'in' just joins it to THE MAP for shuffling.
explanation.definitionFit: A pamphlet is a small booklet issued for publication, often on a topical matter.

clue.text: Caution Glaswegian man taken in by an attractive person

parts.note: an gives A

indicators.note: taken in by means held inside

parts.note: a dish is slang for an attractive person
mon is the Scots form of man

explanation.surface: A warning to a Glasgow man who has been fooled by someone good-looking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in' suggests being fooled, but it is a containment signal; 'mon' is the Scots pronunciation of man.
explanation.definitionFit: To caution someone is to warn or reprove them, which is what admonish means.

clue.text: Gene carrier's doctor thus seen in shiny coat

indicators.note: seen in means placed inside

parts.note: chrome is a shiny metal plating
MO is a Medical Officer, a doctor
so means thus

explanation.surface: A doctor in a shiny coat holding forth about genetics.
explanation.definitionFit: A chromosome is a thread of DNA in a cell nucleus that carries the genes.

clue.text: Rest of the 650?

parts.note: the 650 are the members of the UK House of Commons, and their break from sitting is the rest meant

explanation.walkthrough: 'Rest of' reads as 'the remainder of', but it is a holiday; the House of Commons has 650 MPs.
explanation.definitionFit: Parliament's holiday periods, when MPs are not sitting, are each called a recess.

clue.text: Exercise follows walk in smooth flat land

parts.note: a step is a walk, a pace
PE is physical education, exercise

explanation.surface: A fitness routine of walking and exercise out on open level ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A steppe is a vast treeless grassy plain, as in Russia and Central Asia.

clue.text: Fed gruel initially by staff

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of gruel

parts.note: first letter gives G
to man is to staff

explanation.surface: A workhouse scene: given gruel by the staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fed' looks like a past tense of feed; it is US slang for a federal agent.
explanation.definitionFit: A G-man is a US government agent of the FBI, and a fed is a federal agent.

clue.text: Permit 51 churches to keep name

parts.note: 51 in Roman numerals is LI

indicators.note: to keep means holding inside

parts.note: CE is the Church of England, so two churches give CE twice

explanation.surface: An official permit issued to fifty-one churches, on condition they keep a name.
explanation.definitionFit: A licence is a permit, an official authorisation to do something.

clue.text: Mediocre writer returned Japanese currency in carriage

parts.note: a hack is a writer of mediocre work

indicators.note: returned means turned back, read backwards

parts.note: the yen is Japan's currency

explanation.surface: A jobbing writer handing back yen in a cab.
explanation.walkthrough: Hackney is also a London borough, but here it is a horse-drawn hired carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A hackney is a horse-drawn coach kept for hire, hence the hackney carriage taxi licence.

clue.text: Military leader winning in successful manoeuvre

parts.note: CO is a Commanding Officer
up means ahead, winning

explanation.surface: A general winning the day through a clever manoeuvre.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a military takeover; the definition is the wider sense of a brilliant stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: A coup is a notable success or masterstroke, a brilliantly executed move.

clue.text: Dramatist recalled in Verlaine's biography

indicators.note: recalled says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the answer sits inside the words that follow, spanning them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A playwright mentioned in a biography of the French poet Verlaine.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters are inside 'Verlaine's biography' backwards: S-B-I from the first word into the next.
explanation.definitionFit: Henrik Ibsen was the Norwegian playwright of A Doll's House and Hedda Gabler.

clue.text: New course held by Rolls-Royce after parking sign

indicators.note: after says the car-maker's part follows the parking letter, so that letter comes first
held by means the shuffled letters sit inside the car-maker's initials

parts.note: RR is the badge abbreviation of Rolls-Royce

indicators.note: new says the following word is made over into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A Rolls-Royce taking a new route after passing a parking sign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parking sign' reads as one thing; 'sign' alone is the definition, with 'after' placing P first.
explanation.definitionFit: A precursor is something that comes before and signals what follows, a harbinger or sign.
